'''''Bromus commutatus''''', the '''meadow brome''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is an [[Annual plant|annual]] or [[biennial plant|biennial]]<ref name="H87"/> [[species]] of [[plant]] in the grass [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Poaceae]]. In the United States it is known as '''hairy chess'''.

==Description==
The height ranges from 40 to {{convert|120|cm|0|abbr=on}}. The panicle is 7–20 cm, usually nodding and often spreading,<ref>Clapham, Page 460</ref> but erect as first.<ref name="F74">Fitter, Page 74</ref>  The leaf-sheaths are hairy, the upper are usually hairless.<ref name="F74"/> ''B. commutatus'' is stouter than ''[[Bromus racemosus|B. racemosus]]'', the smooth brome, with a flower-head not drooping to one side and a broader elongated branched flower head.<ref>McLintock, Page 277</ref>

==Habitat and distribution==
It is found in meadows, wasteground, road verges, hayfields and rough grassland.<ref>Philips, Page 72</ref> Found throughout the United Kingdom, it is common in England on the moist soils of water meadows; it is rare in Scotland, Ireland and Wales.<ref name="H87">Hubbard, Page 85</ref> It is found naturally throughout Europe, N. Africa, W. Asia. It has been introduced into North America and in the United States is known as 'Hairy Chess'. The flowering period is from May to July.<ref name="H87"/>

==Crop value==
[[File:Meadow Brome in sward.JPG|left|thumb|upright|Meadow brome in a typical habitat]]
The species has no fodder value in the United Kingdom and is regarded as a weed. The attractive inflorescences may be used, either fresh or dry, in flower arrangements.<ref name="H87"/>

==Varieties==
''Bromus commutatus'' var. ''pubens'' Wats has spikelets which are not hairless, having soft hairs.<ref name="H87"/>
